Remove Outermost Parentheses.problem: Remove the outer pair of each primitive component of a balanced parentheses string.
Remove Outermost Parentheses.approach: Opening at depth zero and closing to depth zero delimit a primitive and are omitted; interior characters are kept.
Remove Outermost Parentheses.pitfalls: A primitive has no proper nonempty balanced prefix. Reject malformed input rather than returning a misleading partial string.

Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses.problem: Return maximum parentheses nesting in an otherwise arbitrary balanced expression.
Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses.approach: Track current open parentheses and maximum depth reached. Nonparenthesis characters do not change depth.
Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses.trace: The ((8)/4) segment sits inside an outer pair, reaching depth 3.
Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses.pitfalls: Malformed parentheses are rejected; an expression without parentheses has depth zero.

Roman to Integer.problem: Convert a valid canonical Roman numeral (normally 1..3999) to integer.
Roman to Integer.approach: A smaller symbol before a larger one is subtractive; all other symbols are additive.
Roman to Integer.pitfalls: This converter assumes valid Roman syntax; it rejects unknown symbols but does not validate canonical repetition rules.

String to Integer (atoi).problem: Skip leading ASCII spaces, accept one optional sign, read consecutive decimal digits, and clamp to signed int range. No digits yields zero.
String to Integer (atoi).approach: Accumulate magnitude. Before multiplying by ten, compare with (limit-digit)/10 so even very long strings cannot overflow the accumulator.
String to Integer (atoi).trace: Skip spaces, read -, accumulate 4 then 42, stop at the following space.
String to Integer (atoi).pitfalls: Negative magnitude permits 2147483648; positive permits only 2147483647. Two signs or a nondigit before digits produce zero.

Count Number of Substrings.problem: Count substrings with exactly k distinct UTF-16 characters.
Count Number of Substrings.approach: Exactly k = atMost(k)-atMost(k-1). Each valid at-most window ending at r contributes r-l+1 suffixes.
Count Number of Substrings.trace: pqpqs has six valid substrings in pqpq with exactly two distinct, plus qs, totaling seven.
Count Number of Substrings.pitfalls: The source title does not specify a variant; this lesson explicitly chooses exactly k distinct. k<=0 returns zero for nonempty substrings.
Count Number of Substrings.alternatives: Directly enumerate substrings and update counts in O(n²) time.

Longest Palindromic Substring.problem: Return a longest contiguous palindrome; ties keep the earliest center discovered.
Longest Palindromic Substring.approach: Every palindrome has an odd center or an even center between characters. Expand both kinds at every index, retaining the longest.
Longest Palindromic Substring.complexity: O(n²) worst time; O(1) auxiliary state plus O(answer length) substring output.
Longest Palindromic Substring.trace: At center a in babad expand b-a-b; later aba ties length 3 and does not replace bab.
Longest Palindromic Substring.pitfalls: Empty input returns empty. Substring and subsequence are different problems.
Longest Palindromic Substring.alternatives: Checking each substring character-by-character costs O(n³). DP takes O(n²) time/space; Manacher can achieve O(n) time.

Sum of Beauty of All Substrings.problem: For lowercase a..z, beauty of a substring is largest minus smallest POSITIVE frequency. Sum over all nonempty substrings.
Sum of Beauty of All Substrings.approach: For each left boundary extend right, updating counts. Scan the fixed alphabet for frequency extrema; this avoids recounting the substring from scratch.
Sum of Beauty of All Substrings.trace: Zero-frequency letters do not affect the minimum; otherwise even a single-character string would incorrectly have positive beauty.
Sum of Beauty of All Substrings.pitfalls: Use long total. Nonlowercase input is rejected.
Sum of Beauty of All Substrings.alternatives: Recounting every substring from scratch takes O(n³) time.
